arxiv-2312-15775.title: Spectral analysis of self-adjoint first order differential operators with nonlocal potentials
arxiv-2312-15775.creator: K. Dębowska, I. L. Nizhnik
arxiv-2312-15775.description: Abstract The paper considers the general form of self-adjoint boundary value problems for momentum operators with nonlocal potentials. We give an analysis of the eigenvalue distribution as zeros of the characteristic functions, for which their explicit representations are obtained in terms of nonlocal potentials. 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification: 34L05, 47E05.

arxiv-2402-08496.title: A Systematic Review of Data-to-Text NLG.
arxiv-2402-08496.creator: Chinonso Cynthia Osuji, Thiago Castro Ferreira, Brian Davis
arxiv-2402-08496.description: Abstract This systematic review undertakes a comprehensive analysis of current research on data-to-text generation, identifying gaps, challenges, and future directions within the field. Relevant literature in this field on datasets, evaluation metrics, application areas, multilingualism, language models, and hallucination mitigation methods is reviewed. Various methods for producing high-quality text are explored, addressing the challenge of hallucinations in data-to-text generation.

arxiv-2505-18217.title: ABHINAYA - A System for Speech Emotion Recognition In Naturalistic Conditions Challenge
arxiv-2505-18217.creator: Soumya, Smruthi, Varada, Viveka, Sriram
arxiv-2505-18217.description: Abstract Speech emotion recognition (SER) in naturalistic settings remains a challenge due to the intrinsic variability, diverse recording conditions, and class imbalance. As participants in the Interspeech Naturalistic SER Challenge which focused on these complexities, we present “Abhinaya”, a system integrating speech-based, text-based, and speech-text models.

arxiv-2509-07796.title: Co-existence of longitudinal and transverse oscillations in polar plumes observed with Solar Orbiter/EUI Journal: ApJL
arxiv-2509-07796.creator: Upasna Baweja, Vaibhav Pant, S. Krishna Prasad, Arpit Kumar Shrivastav, Tom Van Doorsselaere, Nancy Narang, Cis Verbeeck, M. Saleem Khan, David Berghmans
arxiv-2509-07796.description: Abstract Magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) waves play a key role in heating the solar corona and driving the solar wind. Recent observations have shown the presence of slow magneto-acoustic and Alfvénic waves in polar plumes and inter-plumes. However, a complete understanding of wave dynamics in the polar regions has long been limited by the lack of simultaneous, high-resolution observations.

arxiv-2509-17902.title: Entrywise preservers of sign regularity
arxiv-2509-17902.creator: Projesh Nath Choudhury and Shivangi Yadav
arxiv-2509-17902.description: Abstract . Entrywise functions preserving positivity and related notions have a rich history, beginning with the seminal works of Schur, Pólya–Szegő, Schoenberg, and Rudin. Following their classical results, it is well-known that entrywise functions preserving positive semidefiniteness for matrices of all dimensions must be real analytic with non-negative Taylor coefficients.

arxiv-2601-14496.creator: Shi Feng, Nandini Trivedi

In Kitaev’s paradigmatic honeycomb model a spin- 1 2 \tfrac{1}{2} fractionalizes into Z 2 Z_{2} flux due to emergent Z 2 Z_{2} gauge field and matter Majorana fermions.

arxiv-2602-16624.title: Measurement of the Saturation Length of the Self-Modulation Instability
arxiv-2602-16624.creator: A. Clairembaud, M. Turner, M. Bergamaschi, L. Ranc, F. Pannell, J. Mezger, H. Jaworska, N. van Gils, J. Farmer, P. Muggli, AWAKE Collaboration, C.C. Ahdida, Y. Alekajbaf, C. Amoedo, O. Apsimon, R. Apsimon, T. Bachmann, C. Badiali, M. Baquero, E. Belli, A. Boccardi, T. Bogey, S. Burger, P.N. Burrows,
arxiv-2602-16624.description: Abstract The self-modulation (SM) instability transforms a long charged particle bunch traveling in plasma into a train of microbunches that resonantly drives large-amplitude wakefields. We present the first determination of the saturation length of SM using experimental and numerical results. The saturation length is the distance over which wakefields reach their maximum amplitude along the plasma.

pmc-10569690.title: Long-term, repeated doses of intravenous autologous mesenchymal stem cells for a patient with Parkinson's disease: a case report
pmc-10569690.creator: Ridhima Vij, Alan Prossin, Mallika Tripathy, Hosu Kim, Hyeonggeun Park, Thanh Cheng, Djamchid Lotfi, Donna Chang
pmc-10569690.description: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a neurodegenerative disease that involves the loss of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra pars compacta of the basal ganglia. Clinically, patient presentation involves a combination of motor and non-motor symptoms characterized by progressive worsening over time and significant decreases in overall quality-of-life.

pmc-12449671.title: Decoupling Between Functional Diversity and Stability of Decomposer Functions in Natural and Agroecosystems Can Favor Resistance to Land‐Use Change
pmc-12449671.creator: Shamik Roy, Sumanta Bagchi
pmc-12449671.description: Functional diversity in producers and consumers can not only promote ecosystem functions but also impart additional desirable features, such as stability of functions and how they are translated into services. These connections between diversity, functions, and stability are seen across various natural ecosystems in the terrestrial, marine, and freshwater realms.

pmc-12989492.title: Lipid metabolism dysregulation in solar lentigo: a multi-system-level analysis reveals membrane instability and energy homeostasis disruption
pmc-12989492.creator: Sohyun Kim, Wonmin Lee, Junghyun Kim, Yoonsung Lee, Kiwon Lee, Man S. Kim, Soon-Hyo Kwon
pmc-12989492.description: Solar lentigo is a common hyperpigmented skin condition caused by chronic ultraviolet exposure, primarily affecting photoaged skin. While previous investigations focused on inflammatory and melanogenic mechanisms, the comprehensive role of lipid metabolism in pathogenesis remains unclear. We aimed to investigate systemic alterations in lipid metabolism and their contribution to solar lentigo development.

pmc-13288958.title: Tysabri Observational Program (TOP): long-term safety and effectiveness of natalizumab treatment in relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis over 15 years
pmc-13288958.creator: Helmut Butzkueven, Ludwig Kappos, Heinz Wiendl, Maria Trojano, Tim Spelman, Andres Greco, Zhaonan Sun, Tyler Lasky, On behalf of the TOP Investigators
pmc-13288958.description: ObjectiveThis Tysabri Observational Program (TOP) final analysis evaluated the 15-year safety and effectiveness of natalizumab treatment in patients with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (RRMS).MethodsThis multinational, real-world observational study assessed natalizumab-associated serious adverse events, annualised relapse rates (ARRs) and disability progression/improvement in patients with RRMS.

pmc-13297851.title: Reconsideration of Information-Theoretic Principles—Perspective from the Dual Probability Distribution
pmc-13297851.creator: Yoshikazu Ohtaki, Tomomi Nakamura, Hiroshi-H. Hasegawa, Tatsuaki Wada
pmc-13297851.description: We reconsider information-theoretic principles, such as the maximum entropy principle/minimum Massieu potential principle, from the perspective of the dual probability distribution. This is introduced through Sanov’s Lemma for the multinomial distribution. The dual correspondence becomes asymptotically manifest. The Massieu potential is rewritten as the Kullback–Leibler divergence between the dual probability distribution and the dual reference distribution.

pmc-13366672.title: Benchmarking inflammation-nutrition and TyG-related indices for 5-year mortality risk in adults with questionnaire-defined obstructive sleep apnea: a survey-weighted NHANES derivation cohort with multicenter external validation
pmc-13366672.creator: Jian Liu, Huiqian Yang, Zheng Wang, Shaban Ahmad, Shuang Zhou, Lingling Zhou, Dan Lou, Zhiqiang Guo, Hui Li, Xiaoming Li
pmc-13366672.description: BackgroundObstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is associated with excess mortality, and readily obtainable biomarkers may support pragmatic risk stratification in OSA, but their comparative and incremental value remains uncertain. We benchmarked inflammation-nutrition indices and TyG-related metabolic indices for mortality risk in adults with questionnaire-defined OSA and evaluated whether these markers improve 5-year all-cause mortality prediction beyond a basic clinical model.

pmc-13485425.title: A Comparative Analysis of Pig-to-Rhesus Corneal Xenotransplantation with Various Immunosuppressive Regimens
pmc-13485425.creator: Seung Hyeun Lee, Chang Ho Yoon, Hyuk Jin Choi, Hyun Ju Lee, Hee Jung Kang, Jong Min Kim, Chung-Gyu Park, Mee Kum Kim
pmc-13485425.description: PurposePrevious studies had made efforts to find the optimal regimens to reduce xenogeneic rejection in corneal xenotransplantation. However, it had not been fully determined which immunosuppressive choice would be optimal for long-term graft survival. We aimed to compare clinical results in wild-type pig-to-rhesus corneal xenotransplantation with various immunosuppressive regimens.

pmc-13541390.title: Interlocking plate compared with conventional pin fixation for undisplaced femoral neck fractures: a randomized controlled trial with radiostereometric analysis
pmc-13541390.creator: Magnus Høgevold, Michaela Manalili Hansen, Jan Egil Brattgjerd, Stephan Maximillian Röhrl
pmc-13541390.description: AimsIn undisplaced femoral neck fractures, fixation failure remains a concern. In vitro studies suggest that interlocking plates increase torsional stability. However, whether this leads to clinically relevant improvement in fixation stability in vivo remains unclear. Accordingly, we tested whether interlocking plate fixation provides increased in vivo fixation stability over 52 weeks in undisplaced femoral neck fractures.

pmc-13583653.title: Age at Diagnosis and Clinical and Genetic Profiles Among Adults With Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder
pmc-13583653.creator: Douglas Teixeira Leffa, Guilherme Bauer-Negrini, Bruna Bellaver, Firoza Z. Lussier, Pamela C. L. Ferreira, Guilherme Povala, Samuele Cortese, Luis Augusto Rohde, Brooke S. G. Molina, Tharick A. Pascoal
pmc-13583653.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Key PointsQuestionDo demographic, clinical, and genetic profiles of adults diagnosed with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) in adulthood differ from adults diagnosed with ADHD in childhood or adolescence, and how do profiles of both groups compare with matched controls without ADHD?FindingsIn this cross-sectional study of 13 527 adults with ADHD, adult-diagnosed individuals had significantly fewer psychiatric and somatic comorbidities, less impairment in overall health and daily activities, and lower ADHD polygenic risk scores than youth-diagnosed individuals.

pmc-13658335.title: Hybrid approach with convolutional neural network and regression models for age estimation in panoramic radiographs
pmc-13658335.creator: Jhonatan Thiago Lacerda-Santos, José Alberto Souza Paulino, Hiarles Barreto Sampaio Brito, Fabiana Tolentino Almeida, Patrícia Meira Bento, Daniela Pita de Melo
pmc-13658335.description: BackgroundDetermining chronological age is a relevant aspect of criminal and civil interest for identifying corpses and refugees. This study aimed to estimate chronological age using a hybrid model that combines a convolutional neural network (CNN) with regression models based on panoramic radiographs.MethodsThis observational, retrospective and cross-sectional study analyzed 2,546 panoramic radiographs from a Brazilian practice.
